## Security verdict: PASS

PR #192, exact head `ffae78163f60762d894cf9808a623c5091ad018f`.

The complete small diff and flag wiring were source-reviewed. The idle-holder nudge is disabled by default before any nudge-store read, message or FYI. No new security vulnerability was identified.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | No vulnerability identified | - |

`Config::idle_nudge` defaults to false (`crates/core/src/config.rs:188-218`). The daemon composition root reads `PIJ_IDLE_NUDGE` once, accepting trimmed, case-insensitive `1`, `on` or `true`; missing/other values leave it off (`crates/cli/src/main.rs:2704-2711`). The value is copied into Services at construction (`crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:200,655`), not read from a seat or per round.

`idle_nudge::round` returns before accessing the store when off (`crates/daemon/src/idle_nudge.rs:61-65`). The PA watchdog's runtime call uses that function (`crates/daemon/src/pa_watchdog.rs:492`); no new HTTP or seat-controlled opt-in was added. The enabled algorithm is unchanged.

The default-config test supplies an idle holder and asserts no outcome, message or parent FYI; existing tests explicitly enable the feature (`crates/daemon/src/idle_nudge_tests.rs:19-39,269-287`). Those assertions were read, not locally executed.

API, PA brief and D-F144-1 accurately describe default-off part 1 rather than claiming the in-flight-work/cold-wake policy fix is complete. The PR deliberately has no Fixes line so coder/f144 remains for part 2. No migration, new launch or C19/C21 disclosure was identified.

GitHub metadata and the independent remote pull ref agree on the full reviewed SHA; GitHub reports CLEAN. CI run `42507561673` and Delivers run `42507561683` both identify this SHA and success.

No local builds, tests, nudge/daemon operations, environment changes, credential reads or mutations were performed.
